direct_primary_context.literal_passage:
POWER AND FEAR EFFECTS
DAMAGE, DESTRUCTION, AND REMOVAL
Some effects remove Invaders, representing them fleeing in terror. Return the specified pieces to the 
supply. Some replace Invaders: first you remove the Invader, then you put something else in its place. 
A replaced Invader keeps any Damage it had. More Powers destroy Invaders outright. Return the 
specified pieces to the supply. Destroying a Town generates 1 Fear and destroying a City generates 2 
Fear, but removing or replacing does not.
Whenever a Power or other effect says “Damage”, it always means “Damage to Invaders” unless 
explicitly specified otherwise. When dealing Damage, it is done to any Invaders in the target land, 
divided among them however you choose. If an Invader has taken Damage equal to or greater than 
its Health (see Invaders, page 15), it is destroyed immediately. Damage may be combined from
multiple Powers. However, any remaining Damage on survivors heals at the end of the turn.
DEFEND
Some Powers let you Defend a target land, which reduces Damage done by Invaders to the land 
and/or Dahan. “Defend 2” means “Whenever Invaders deal Damage in target land this turn, reduce 
by 2 the Damage done to the land and to Dahan.” If multiple Defend effects are used in one land, 
they add together. Defend effects last for the entire turn. There are optional tokens you can use to 
help you remember that a land is Defended this turn.
REMOVING BLIGHT
When you remove Blight from the Island, return it to the Blight Card, on whichever side is currently 
face-up. The Blight Card will not flip from Blighted back to Healthy during the timespan of the game, 
no matter how much Blight you remove.
GAME CONCEPTS
WHAT POWER CARDS CAN I FORGET?
Any of your cards! From your hand, your discard,
or (if you somehow gain a Major Power mid-turn)
from your cards in play. It can even be the Major 
Power you just chose. If you Forget a Power Card
from play, you immediately lose the Elements it
provided, and if you haven’t used it yet, you don’t
get to. If you already used it, its effects continue
until end of turn as usual.
DAMAGE HURTS INVADERS
Invaders are not the only recipients of Damage in
Spirit Island: the land and Dahan can take Damage
from Invaders Ravaging. But the overwhelming
majority of Damage in the game is done to Invaders.
Any time a Power, Fear Card, or other game rule
does Damage, it always means “Damage to Invaders”
unless explicitly specified otherwise. Most Spirit
Powers do not harm the land or Dahan.
DAMAGE TOKENS?
There are no tokens in Spirit Island for tracking
Damage. Instead models are built to be rotated
to help track Damage done to them.
(For more details, see sidebars on page 15 and 16.)
FEAR FROM DESTRUCTION
Whenever a City or Town is destroyed (via
Damage or otherwise), it frightens the Invaders.
You generate 2 Fear for each City destroyed and
1 Fear for each Town destroyed (in addition to
any Fear done explicitly by the Power).
If you remove or replace a City/Town, it does not
generate this automatic Fear.
DEFEND SIDE OF REMINDER TOKENS

primary_text.label: full illegal-location cleanup procedure
primary_text.literal_passage:
What happens if a piece winds up in a place or state it's not allowed to be?
(.7w4gdtl)
If the place still exists, then:
Pieces representing humans
(Dahan / Invaders) are
cleaned up
to the closest legal land — this is not considered a move, is not an action, and does not trigger anything, it is simply a correction of the game state. This happens only once you are not in the middle of an action, and there are no pending triggered actions (i.e., after each action tree), just before checking for victory/defeat.
All other pieces
remain where they are, but are considered out of play unless/until they're no longer in an illegal state.
On the other hand, if the place was destroyed and pieces within it somehow survived the destruction, they all get cleaned up.
This sort of thing can happen if pieces survive the sinking of a board (like Dahan via
Infinite Vitality
with threshold or Explorers via the Tsardom of Russia's
A Sense for Impending Disaster
(.9v5kfpm)
), if an Ocean stops being a land (by Ocean's Hungry Grasp losing its Presence there) while other Spirits' Presence is there, or if Invaders/Dahan are left in the Ocean after an action but manage not to Drown in some way.
If the nearest legal land is unclear, use your best judgment, based on physical distance if necessary. If there is literally no legal land to put the pieces in, return them to the supply; this is still considered
cleaning up
(not an action, not a move/remove/destroy, does not trigger anything).

literal_actual_ask_overlaps.question: Does every watery destruction count as Drowning? If Ocean’s last Presence on a board is lost mid-action, when does Ocean In Play expire and what happens to other Spirits’ Presence and surviving humans left there?
If a human piece remains illegally placed after an action tree, how is it cleaned up? Is that a move, destroy, remove or action, and what if no legal land exists?

An Invader is left illegally in an Ocean after its primary action and all triggered actions finish. Assume it was not Drowned. May it remain there, where is it placed instead, and does that relocation count as movement or trigger movement effects?

Ocean In Play is active on a board. Infinite Vitality with its threshold protects Dahan in that Ocean, and a Power Pushes a Dahan into it. Ocean In Play triggers but cannot destroy that Dahan. With an adjacent non-Ocean land available, what happens next: does the Dahan remain until cleanup, or is it Pushed? Is that relocation an actual Push within the triggered action or merely cleanup?

After a primary action and all triggered actions finish, an Invader is still illegally placed. Do players check victory/defeat with that illegal position first, or correct its position before that check? Assume a legal destination exists.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: For two Spirits, how are the Fear pool/deck and Invader deck prepared, what initial Blight pool is used with and without a Blight Card, and what final Invader action completes setup?

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: For two Spirits, how are the Fear pool/deck and Invader deck prepared, what initial Blight pool is used with and without a Blight Card, and what final Invader action completes setup?
required_facts: Two Spirits use 8 Fear markers.
Shuffle and use 9 Fear cards in three groups of 3 separated by Terror II/III.
Prepare 3 random Stage I above 4 Stage II above 5 Stage III, removing one unseen card of each stage.
Initial Healthy pool is 5; initial no-card pool is 11, including exactly one setup bonus.
Finish setup with a normal Explore and leave that card face-up in Build.

unasked_key_context_not_used_as_tested_c.fact: Ravage is initially empty.
unasked_key_context_not_used_as_tested_c.why_not_requested: Helpful initial-board context; the requested final setup action is Explore and its placement.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.predetermined_current_answer: Use 8 Fear markers, 9 shuffled Fear cards divided 3/3/3 by Terror II and III dividers; Invader deck is 3 Stage I above 4 Stage II above 5 Stage III, randomized within each stage with one unused card per stage removed unseen. Initial Blight is 5 with a Healthy Island card (2 per player +1), or 11 without (5 per player +1). Setup Explore the top card normally and leave it face-up in Build; Ravage is initially empty.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: A Spirit chooses Growth with two Add Presence actions. May the second placement use the first as its range origin? Which Presence-track disks may be taken, and how do uncovered Energy/Card Plays numbers combine?
required_facts: Resolve the two placement actions in chosen order; the first new Presence may originate the second.
Take the leftmost remaining disk of either selected track for each placement.
Only the highest uncovered Energy and Card Plays numbers apply; do not add numbers.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.predetermined_current_answer: Yes; resolve Growth actions in chosen order, so the first placement can extend the second. Each placement takes the leftmost remaining Presence from either chosen track. Use only the highest uncovered Energy number and highest uncovered Card Plays number, not their sum.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: A Spirit has no Presence on its tracks but has Presence on the island and some destroyed disks. How can an Add Presence instruction be resolved, where is range measured, and can destroyed disks be used?

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: A Spirit has no Presence on its tracks but has Presence on the island and some destroyed disks. How can an Add Presence instruction be resolved, where is range measured, and can destroyed disks be used?
required_facts: With tracks empty, reposition one of that Spirit's island Presence.
Measure the legal destination from existing island Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, before picking a disk up.
Any of its island disks may supply the placement.
Destroyed disks cannot supply ordinary Add Presence without explicit permission.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.predetermined_current_answer: Reposition one of its island Presence instead of taking a track disk. First choose a legal destination measured from existing island Presence, including the disk about to be repositioned, then take any of its island disks. Destroyed Presence is unavailable unless explicitly allowed.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: When are Fast and Slow Power Cards paid for and their Elements gained? Can promised Fast-phase Energy pay for the Spirit-phase cards, and do unspent Energy or unused Card Plays carry over?

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: When are Fast and Slow Power Cards paid for and their Elements gained? Can promised Fast-phase Energy pay for the Spirit-phase cards, and do unspent Energy or unused Card Plays carry over?
required_facts: Play and pay for both Fast and Slow cards during Spirit Phase.
Their Elements become available immediately on play/payment.
Fast-phase Energy arrives too late to pay these normal Spirit-phase costs.
Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.predetermined_current_answer: Play and pay for all cards in the Spirit Phase, gaining their Elements immediately, including Slow cards. Later Fast-phase Energy cannot pay these earlier costs. Unspent Energy carries over; unused Card Plays do not.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: May a Fast Power wait until Slow, may Powers interrupt each other, and when must a Slow Power’s target be selected?

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: May a Fast Power wait until Slow, may Powers interrupt each other, and when must a Slow Power’s target be selected?
required_facts: Fast Powers must resolve in Fast or be foregone; they cannot wait until Slow.
Finish one Power before another; Powers cannot interrupt one another.
Choose a Slow Power's target when it is used in Slow, using the then-current position and restrictions.

unasked_key_context_not_used_as_tested_c.fact: Players may choose the sequence of different Powers within the appropriate phase.
unasked_key_context_not_used_as_tested_c.why_not_requested: Whether Powers may interrupt each other asks non-interruption, not the independent permission to choose the sequence of different Powers.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.predetermined_current_answer: A Fast Power must be used during Fast or foregone; it cannot wait until Slow. Players choose Power order but finish one before another. Choose the Slow target when using the Power in Slow, using the then-current legal range and target, not irrevocably at card play.

current_actual_ask_and_fact_checks.literal_question: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.

literal_requested_clauses_and_required_f.actual_requested_clause: In a Ravage a land has one Town, one Explorer and two undamaged Dahan, with no Defend or prior Blight. Resolve damage to land, Dahan, surviving counterattack and resulting Fear if the players destroy the Town.
required_facts: Town plus Explorer deal 3 Damage simultaneously to land and Dahan.
Add one Blight to the previously unblighted land.
Destroy one Dahan efficiently and mark 1 Damage on the survivor.
The surviving Dahan still deals 2 counterattack Damage.
Destroying the chosen Town generates 1 Fear.

unasked_key_context_not_used_as_tested_c.why_not_requested: The question ends with this Ravage and resulting Fear, not end-of-turn healing.

The surviving Dahan still deals 2 Damage, destroying the Town and generating 1 Fear. Dahan do not absorb/prevent land damage; partial Dahan damage clears at Time Passes.
